recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source change is needed for FHIR-28938; if OO later wants a reusable SoftwareSystem profile or dedicated SoftwareSystemType terminology, it should be handled as new work rather than as this applied issue.
issue_request: FHIR-28938 originally requested adding the Quality Measures SoftwareSystem Device profile to FHIR core. The final Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution for R6 instead required DeviceDefinition scope/boundary text to clearly cover hardware and software, the registered-name definition from FHIR-20639 to be adjusted, and Device.type SNOMED examples to include more hardware/software branches.
initial_application: The source application was commit f6322c5a6098b5ebcd461371f5038bd584703d0c, merged by 7f1e8ddfc7cdf5502e73f831d3802d4c92c6ecfa through HL7/fhir#3118. It updated source/device/codesystem-device-nametype.xml, added SNOMED CT 706689003 to source/device/valueset-device-type.xml, and added initial Device software wording. Later Device/DeviceDefinition narrative work, especially 43ec2e63cec03fdf90091d9ce7ffc329004bb2e7, moved and expanded the software explanation into DeviceDefinition.
additional_context: The 2025-10-30 OO on FHIR minutes record that the prior SoftwareSystemType disposition could not be applied because SoftwareSystemType was not helpful to include and Device.type has only example bindings; the group confirmed all other disposition points were pre-applied and voted Persuasive with Modification 9-0-0. Jira was subsequently updated to the narrower Applied resolution. Searches found no separate Jira for SoftwareSystemType and no directly relevant Zulip discussion that changed the conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Current source/fhir.ini includes Device and DeviceDefinition in the build; current DeviceDefinition and Device narrative text cover software, the revised registered-name definition is present, and Device.type includes the SNOMED CT 706689003 branch.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-28938 explicitly reused and adjusted the registered-name definition from this published Device.name.type issue. It was context only and was not independently decided.
